name: AiTells

rules.name: AbstractTriad
rules.message: Abstract-noun triad '%s': name one concrete thing instead of three abstractions.

rules.name: Adverb
rules.message: Filler adverb '%s': let the verb carry it.

rules.name: Cliche
rules.message: Cliche '%s': cut it or say the literal thing.

rules.name: CodeToken

rules.name: CopulaInflation
rules.message: Copula inflation '%s': use a plain verb.

rules.name: Dash
rules.message: Em/en dash: recast with a period, comma, colon, or 'to' for a range.

rules.name: EpigramContrast
rules.message: Epigram contrast '%s': cut the negated half; the positive claim is stronger.

rules.name: FilePath
rules.message: Raw file path '%s' in prose: name the document by its human title.

rules.name: HiddenVerb
rules.message: Hidden verb '%s': use the direct verb (analyze, not conduct an analysis).

rules.name: LinkText
rules.message: Vague link text '%s': describe the destination.

rules.name: NegParallel
rules.message: 'not just X, but Y' escalation: say Y.

rules.name: NeverTag
rules.message: ', never X' antithesis tag: state the behavior once and stop.

rules.name: Passive
rules.message: Passive voice '%s': name who does the verb.

rules.name: SectionCode
rules.message: Section/source code '%s' in prose: name it, do not cite a code.

rules.name: StatusBracket
rules.message: Status bracket '%s': keep grades in a source-notes block, not inline prose.

rules.name: VirtueHonest
rules.message: Claimed honesty '%s': cut the claim and state the thing plainly.

rules.name: WeakResume
rules.message: Weak duty-phrasing '%s': lead with a quantified outcome (X by Y measured Z).

name: Commits
description: Commit messages: nine conventions and the rule sets of commitlint, gitlint, committed, conform, and commitizen, read through a View.

rules.name: Blank
rules.message: Separate the subject from the body with a blank line.

rules.name: Body
rules.message: Commit body is empty.

rules.name: Body
rules.message: A body is mandatory except for 'docs', and runs at least 20 characters: explain why.

rules.name: Body
rules.message: A body is required: say why.

rules.name: BodyCase
rules.message: body-case is lower-case: '%s'.

rules.name: BodyFullStop
rules.message: body-full-stop: the body does not end with a period.

rules.name: BodyIsMissing
rules.message: B6 body-is-missing.

rules.name: BodyLength
rules.message: A body line runs past 100 characters from '%s'.

rules.name: BodyMatchRegex
rules.message: B8 body-match-regex: the body does not match the required pattern.

rules.name: BodyMaxLength
rules.message: A body of %d characters, past body-max-length.

rules.name: BodyMaxLineLength
rules.message: B1 body-max-line-length: this line runs past 80 from '%s'.

rules.name: BodyMinLength
rules.message: B5 body-min-length: a body of %d characters.

rules.name: BodyMinLength
rules.message: A body of %d characters, under body-min-length.

rules.name: BodyTrailingWhitespace
rules.message: B2 body-trailing-whitespace.

rules.name: Breaking
rules.message: '%s' is the one token the spec reads case-sensitively: write 'BREAKING CHANGE:'.

rules.name: BreakingBang
rules.message: A 'BREAKING CHANGE:' footer goes with a '!' in the header.

rules.name: Capital
rules.message: The summary completes 'This change modifies Go to ...', so it does not start with a capital: '%s'.

rules.name: Capitalize
rules.message: Capitalize the subject line: '%s'.

rules.name: Capitalized
rules.message: The summary is not capitalized: '%s'.

rules.name: Case
rules.message: A label is in capitals: '%s'.

rules.name: Closes
rules.message: A Closes: tag takes a URL to the public report, not '%s'.

rules.name: Commit
rules.message: Refer to a commit by twelve or more characters of its SHA-1 and its summary: 'commit e21d2170f366 ("video: remove ...")'.

rules.name: DCO
rules.message: Commit does not have a valid DCO: 'Signed-off-by: Name <email>'.

rules.name: Description
rules.message: A description follows the type: what the change does.

rules.name: DescriptionCapitalized
rules.message: subject_capitalized: '%s'.

rules.name: DescriptionLength
rules.message: Conventional commit description is %d characters, over descriptionLength.

rules.name: DisallowCleanupCommits
rules.message: CC2 contrib-disallow-cleanup-commits: '%s'.

rules.name: Exclamation
rules.message: No '!' before the colon; mark a breaking change with a 'BREAKING CHANGE:' footer.

rules.name: Fixes
rules.message: A Fixes: tag carries at least 12 characters of the SHA-1 and the summary in parentheses: 'Fixes: 54a4f0239f2e ("KVM: MMU: ...")'.

rules.name: Footer
rules.message: '%s' is a footer. Put a blank line between the body and the footers.

rules.name: FooterLength
rules.message: A footer line runs past 100 characters from '%s'.

rules.name: FooterMaxLength
rules.message: Footers of %d characters, past footer-max-length.

rules.name: FooterRequired
rules.message: A footer is required.

rules.name: FullStop
rules.message: A subject does not end with a period.

rules.name: HardLineLength
rules.message: hard_line_length: this line runs past 100 from '%s'.

rules.name: HardTab
rules.message: T4/B3 hard-tab: a tab character.

rules.name: HeaderCase
rules.message: Commit header case is not lower: '%s'.

rules.name: HeaderCase
rules.message: header-case is lower-case: '%s'.

rules.name: HeaderLength
rules.message: Header is %d characters.

rules.name: HeaderLength
rules.message: A header of %d characters, past header-max-length.

rules.name: HeaderMinLength
rules.message: A header of %d characters, under header-min-length.

rules.name: Imperative
rules.message: Write the subject as a command: 'Add', not '%s'.

rules.name: Intention
rules.message: Begin with a gitmoji, as the emoji or its ':shortcode:', then a space. '%s' is not one.

rules.name: InvalidLastCharacter
rules.message: Commit header ends in an invalid character.

rules.name: Issue
rules.message: Reference an issue as 'Fixes #12345' or 'Updates #12345', not '%s'.

rules.name: Jira
rules.message: Commit header does not contain a Jira issue key from the configured projects.

rules.name: Key
rules.message: Include the issue key in the subject, in capitals: 'PROJ-123'.

rules.name: Length
rules.message: A summary of %d characters; the kernel asks for no more than 70-75.

rules.name: Limit
rules.message: A subject of %d characters. Shoot for 50; 72 is the hard limit.

rules.name: LineLength
rules.message: line_length: this line runs past 72 from '%s'.

rules.name: Lowercase
rules.message: A type is lower-case: '%s'.

rules.name: MergeCommit
rules.message: merge_commit: '%s'.

rules.name: Message
rules.message: A message follows the intention: what the change does.

rules.name: NoFixup
rules.message: no_fixup: '%s'.

rules.name: NoWip
rules.message: no_wip: '%s'.

rules.name: Package

rules.name: Period

rules.name: Placeholder

rules.name: References

rules.name: Revert

rules.name: Scope

rules.name: Scope

rules.name: ScopeCase

rules.name: ScopeDelimiter

rules.name: Sentence

rules.name: SignedOff

rules.name: Space

rules.name: SubjectCapitalized

rules.name: SubjectCase

rules.name: SubjectLength

rules.name: SubjectLength
rules.message: A subject of %d characters, outside subject-min-length and subject-max-length.

rules.name: SubjectNotPunctuated

rules.name: Subsystem

rules.name: ThisPatch

name: Elastic
description: Elastic Docs' style guide rules for the Vale linter.

rules.name: Accessibility
rules.message: Don't use language (such as '%s') that defines people by their disability.

rules.name: Articles
rules.message: Use '%s' instead of '%s'. The article depends on pronunciation, not spelling.

rules.name: BritishSpellings
rules.message: Use American English spelling '%s' instead of British English '%s'.

rules.name: Clone
rules.message: Use `%s` only when referring to cloning a GitHub repository or creating a copy that is linked to the original. Often confused with 'copy' and 'duplicate'.

rules.name: ConflictMarkers
rules.message: Do not commit Git merge conflict markers in source code.

rules.name: DeviceAgnosticism
rules.message: Use device-agnostic language when possible. Use '%s' instead of '%s'.

rules.name: Dimensions
rules.message: Avoid using dimensions in the format 'M X N'. Use 'MxN' instead.

rules.name: DirectionalLanguage
rules.message: Don't use directional language. Use '%s' instead of '%s'.

rules.name: DontUse
rules.message: Don't use '%s'. Choose a more precise or reader-focused term.

rules.name: Ellipses
rules.message: Use ellipses sparingly. Remove the ellipsis unless it appears in UI text.

rules.name: EndPuntuaction
rules.message: Don't end headings with punctuation.

rules.name: Exclamation
rules.message: Use exclamation points sparingly. Remove the exclamation point unless it appears in UI text.

rules.name: FirstPerson
rules.message: Use first-person pronouns sparingly. Rephrase '%s' if the sentence can focus on the user or product instead.

rules.name: Gender
rules.message: Don't use '%s'.

rules.name: GenderBias
rules.message: Consider using '%s' instead of '%s'.

rules.name: HeadingColons
rules.message: Capitalize '%s'.

rules.name: KibanaChromeTerms
rules.message: Consider using '%s' instead of '%s' when referring to parts of the Kibana chrome.

rules.name: Latinisms
rules.message: Latin terms and abbreviations are a common source of confusion. Use '%s' instead of '%s'.

rules.name: MappedPages
rules.message: Avoid editing mapped_pages unless you are preserving an existing URL mapping. Talk with your local technical writer before changing this key.

rules.name: MeaningfulCTAs
rules.message: Use meaningful link text. Use '%s' instead of '%s'.

rules.name: MenuArrows
rules.message: Use '→' to separate menu items, not '>' or '=>'. Example: Select Manage index → Add lifecycle policy.

rules.name: MenuArrowsBold
rules.message: Use '→' to separate menu items, not '>' or '=>'. Example: Select Manage index → Add lifecycle policy.

rules.name: Negations
rules.message: Consider rephrasing to avoid negative constructions like '%s'. Try stating what something IS rather than what it is NOT.

rules.name: OxfordComma
rules.message: Use the Oxford comma in '%s'.

rules.name: PluralAbbreviations
rules.message: Don't use apostrophes when making abbreviations plural. Use '%s' instead of '%s'.

rules.name: QuotesPunctuation
rules.message: Place punctuation inside closing quotation marks.

rules.name: Repetition
rules.message: "%s" is repeated.

rules.name: Semicolons
rules.message: Use semicolons sparingly. Consider splitting the sentence or using a comma or conjunction.

rules.name: Spelling
rules.message: '%s' is a possible misspelling.

rules.name: Versions
rules.message: Use '%s' instead of '%s' when referring to versions.

rules.name: WordChoice
rules.message: Consider using '%s' instead of '%s', unless the term is in the UI.

rules.name: Wordiness
rules.message: Consider using '%s' instead of '%s'.

rules.name: FirstPerson

rules.message: Consider using '%s' instead of '%s'.

name: Harper
description: A Vale-compatible implementation of the Harper grammar checker.

rules.name: ACoupleMore
rules.message: The correct wording is `a couple more`, without the `of`.

rules.name: Addicting
rules.message: When used as an adjective, `addictive` is the traditional and more f form.

rules.name: AdjectiveDoubleDegree
rules.message: Did you mean the adjective on its own?

rules.name: AdNauseam
rules.message: This phrase comes from Latin, where `ad` means `to`.

rules.name: AfterAll
rules.message: Did you mean `after all`?

rules.name: AfterAWhile
rules.message: When describing a timeframe, use `a while`.

rules.name: AfterLater
rules.message: `after` and `later` are redundant together.

rules.name: AheadAnd
rules.message: Did you make a typo? Shouldn't it be `and`?

rules.name: Albeit
rules.message: This should be written as a single word with a single `l`: `albeit`.

rules.name: ALittleOfPractice
rules.message: Have you perhaps confused `a little practice` or `a bit of practice`?

rules.name: AllHellBreakLoose
rules.message: The correct idiom is `all hell breaks loose`.

rules.name: AllIntentsAndPurposes
rules.message: The idiom is `for all intents and purposes`.

rules.name: AllOfASudden
rules.message: Prefer the standard phrasing `all of a sudden`.

rules.name: AllowTo1
rules.message: Flags erroneous usage of `allow to` without a subject.

rules.name: AllowTo2
rules.message: Flags erroneous usage of `allow to` without a subject.

rules.name: AllReady
rules.message: Use `already` before adjectives instead of the two-word phrase.

rules.name: AllThough
rules.message: Merge `all` and `though` into the conjunction `although`.

rules.name: Alongside
rules.message: Use the single word `alongside`.

rules.name: ALongTime
rules.message: Use `a long time` for referring to a duration of time.

rules.name: AlzheimersDisease
rules.message: Use the correct medical term.

rules.name: AMeansToAnEnd
rules.message: The correct idiom is `a means to an end`.

rules.name: AmInTheMorning
rules.message: The time period is redundant because it repeats what's already specified by the AM/PM indicator.

rules.name: AmountsFor
rules.message: `amounts for` is not idiomatic English. You probably meant `amounts to` or `accounts for`.

rules.name: AnAnother
rules.message: Use `another` on its own.

rules.name: AndSuch
rules.message: Did you mean `and such`?

rules.name: AndTheLike
rules.message: If you intended the idiom meaning `similar things`, the correct form is with `the like`.

rules.name: AnotherAn
rules.message: Use `another` on its own.

rules.name: AnotherOnes
rules.message: `another` is singular but `ones` is plural. Or maybe you meant the possessive `one's`.

rules.name: AnotherThingComing
rules.message: Corrects `another think coming` to `another thing coming`

rules.name: AnotherThings
rules.message: `another` is singular but `things` is plural.

rules.name: AOkHyphen
rules.message: Use `A-OK` when stating that something is acceptable or ready.

rules.name: ApartFrom
rules.message: Use `from` to spell `apart from`.

rules.name: AsComparedTo
rules.message: Did you mean `as compared to`?

rules.name: AsEvidentBy
rules.message: Did you mean `evidenced`? The correct phrase uses the past participle of the verb `evidence`.

rules.name: AsFarBackAs
rules.message: Use `as far back as` for referring to a time in the past.

rules.name: AsFollows
rules.message: Use `as follows`.

rules.name: AsHow
